description:
We are a team of two looking for more members!

I study Mechatronics Engineering, have basic skills in programming and circuits, and love researching space and new ideas. My teammate studies Computer Engineering, focusing on cybersecurity, ethical hacking, and databases.

We are especially looking for people interested in web development and programming, but all skills, backgrounds, and experience levels are welcome.

If you love collaborating and want to learn together, join us!
summary:
We developed an interactive Mars survival map that lets users create their own exploration routes. As users select points on the map, they can see the latitude, longitude, and elevation of each location. The map connects these points to form a custom route and provides historical temperature and radiation data to help users understand the Martian environment.

Our project addresses the challenge by making it easier to explore different ways of traveling between craters or other regions on Mars. In the future, this approach could help teams plan journeys from a Martian base and prepare for the terrain and conditions they might encounter.

We plan to add routes previously explored by the Perseverance and Curiosity rovers. These routes could serve as references for understanding local terrain and identifying challenges to consider when planning future human exploration.
details:
We developed She Space-Mars, an interactive 3D web map that lets users explore the Martian surface and create their own routes. Users can zoom in, change the viewing angle, and select points on the map. For each selected point, the map displays its latitude, longitude, and elevation. The map connects the points in the order they are selected, so users can build a route between locations they want to explore. The platform also displays historical temperature and radiation data to give users context about conditions on Mars.

Our creative approach was to take something familiar, drawing a route on a digital map, and adapt it to another planet. For example, a student could trace a route between two craters and compare the elevations along the way. This gives students, teachers, and space enthusiasts a hands-on way to learn about Mars and consider the kinds of information that matter when planning an expedition. We also hope the project encourages more girls and young women to see science, engineering, and space exploration as paths they can pursue.

We built the web interface with React, used JavaScript for the map interactions and route logic, and used HTML and CSS to structure and style the application. CesiumJS powers the interactive 3D map. We worked in Visual Studio Code and used Git and GitHub to share code and track changes across the team.

During development, we considered how to make the map easy to use in a browser, how the interface would adapt to different screen sizes, and what scientific data was available. One decision was to update elevation as users select different points and present temperature and radiation as historical reference data. In a future version, we would like to add routes traveled by Curiosity and Perseverance so users can compare their own routes with terrain that rovers have already explored.
